question: According to current NACO syndromic management guidelines, ciprofloxacin is a recommended first-line treatment for urethral/cervical discharge syndrome caused by gonorrhoea in India.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Ciprofloxacin has been dropped from NACO guidelines due to extensive fluoroquinolone resistance in N. gonorrhoeae. The current recommended regimen is ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose (plus azithromycin 1 g orally to cover co-infection with chlamydia).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Ciprofloxacin is NO LONGER recommended for gonorrhoea in India. Widespread fluoroquinolone resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae has rendered it ineffective. Current NACO guidelines recommend ceftriaxone (injectable) ± azithromycin for gonococcal infections.
